caption: The foundation circle of the round tower at Liathmore, with one of the two ruined churches in the background. Saint Mochoemog founded a monastery here in the 7th century and gave his name to our village school.

The Liathmore sheela-na-gig, a small medieval carved figure tucked into the doorway of the larger church. Heavy lichen and centuries of Tipperary weather have softened the stone, but the carving is still there for those who know to look.
A detail of the medieval stonework inside the larger 12th-century church at Liathmore. The carved decoration on the doorway has been quietly weathering since long before our village was here.
